title: Impact of AI-Blended Learning and AI-Personalized Learning on Undergraduate Biology Students' Attitude and Performance in Climate Change Education
venue: Anchor University Journal of Science and Technology
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether AI-enhanced instructional approaches improve undergraduate biology students’ attitudes toward climate change and their academic performance in climate change education better than traditional classroom teaching. The study is motivated by the concern that conventional instruction may not sufficiently engage students or address diverse learning needs when teaching complex environmental topics.

The intervention compared three instructional conditions: AI-Blended Learning, AI-Personalized Learning, and Traditional Classroom Instruction. In the AI-Blended Learning condition, students used ChatGPT-3.5 alongside face-to-face teaching. In the AI-Personalized Learning condition, students relied on ChatGPT-3.5 as the primary instructional support in a fully AI-driven personalized environment. The comparison group received conventional face-to-face instruction without the AI intervention. Outcomes were measured using a Climate Change Attitude Assessment (CCAA) and a Climate Change Achievement Test (CCAT), with pretest and posttest scores analyzed using ANCOVA.

The study involved 70 300-level undergraduate biology students at Federal University Gusau in Nigeria. Students were drawn from existing classes and assigned into three groups: AI-Blended Learning (20), AI-Personalized Learning (20), and Traditional Classroom Instruction (30). The intervention lasted four weeks and covered climate change topics such as causes, impacts, mitigation strategies, and policy actions.

The main finding is that AI-Blended Learning produced substantially stronger gains in both attitude and performance than either AI-Personalized Learning or Traditional Classroom Instruction. Post hoc analyses showed that the blended approach significantly outperformed both alternatives, while AI-Personalized Learning did not significantly differ from traditional instruction on the reported comparisons. The paper concludes that integrating ChatGPT-3.5 with teacher-led classroom instruction is more effective than relying on AI alone, and recommends that higher education lecturers adopt AI-blended approaches to improve engagement and learning outcomes in environmental education.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on the GPT family, used for conversational instruction, question answering, and generating human-like text.
identified_tools.use_case: ChatGPT was the intervention tool in both treatment arms: in AI-Blended Learning it was used alongside face-to-face classroom instruction, and in AI-Personalized Learning it was used as the sole instructional tool for undergraduate biology students learning climate change topics over four weeks.

findings.finding_summary: In the AI-Blended Learning condition using ChatGPT alongside classroom instruction, students showed substantially higher achievement gains in climate change education than the AI-Personalized Learning and Traditional Classroom Instruction groups. Posttest performance for AI-Blended Learning was Mean=27.57 (SD=4.12) versus 16.50 (SD=3.75) for AI-Personalized Learning and 19.01 (SD=3.89) for Traditional Classroom Instruction; ANCOVA showed a significant group effect, F(2,67)=42.281, p<0.001, partial eta squared=0.664, with Scheffé mean differences of 11.66 and 8.68, respectively.
findings.measure: Climate Change Achievement Test (CCAT) posttest scores

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT used in an AI-Blended Learning format significantly improved students' attitudes toward climate change relative to AI-Personalized Learning and Traditional Classroom Instruction. Mean attitude gain was 32.41 for AI-Blended Learning versus 5.16 for AI-Personalized Learning and 3.94 for Traditional Classroom Instruction; ANCOVA found a significant group effect, F(2,67)=144.050, p<0.001, partial eta squared=0.681, and Scheffé tests showed significant differences between AI-Blended Learning and each comparison group.
findings.measure: Climate Change Attitude Assessment (CCAA) posttest scores / mean gain scores

findings.finding_summary: When ChatGPT was used as the sole instructional mode in the AI-Personalized Learning group, student performance did not differ significantly from Traditional Classroom Instruction. The AI-Personalized Learning group had a mean gain score of 0.03 and posttest Mean=16.50 (SD=3.75) versus Traditional Classroom Instruction mean gain of 3.01 and posttest Mean=19.01 (SD=3.89); Scheffé mean difference was 2.98, p>0.05.
findings.measure: Climate Change Achievement Test (CCAT) posttest scores / mean gain scores

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT used alone in the AI-Personalized Learning group did not significantly improve students' attitudes toward climate change compared with Traditional Classroom Instruction. The AI-Personalized Learning group had a mean gain score of 5.16 versus 3.94 for Traditional Classroom Instruction; Scheffé mean difference was 5.22 and was reported as not significant.
findings.measure: Climate Change Attitude Assessment (CCAA) posttest scores / mean gain scores

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study with a comparison group and ANCOVA adjustment, which is stronger than descriptive research but not a randomized controlled trial. The sample is modest (n=70) and reporting is limited to one institution.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported effects for the blended ChatGPT condition are large and statistically significant, with partial eta squared values of 0.681 for attitudes and 0.664 for performance. These indicate substantial impact for the blended implementation, even though the AI-only condition showed null results versus traditional instruction.
